sources.description: lib/learning-paths (FDE, DSA Foundations), gated by env switches
Supabase override table (admin edits, custom questions, hides). Not readable from the repository.
lib/quiz-data.ts coreQuestions outside code-snippets: module-private, exported nowhere

items.objective: Apply the cascade: a more specific selector (.card p, 0-1-1) beats a less specific one (p, 0-0-1) before source order is considered.
defects: hint is the generic fallback ("Name the requirement or behavior first…")
explanation does not say that a losing declaration is still valid CSS, only not applied (option D)
items.rationale: Key verified by hand: .card p = 0-1-0 + 0-0-1 = 0-1-1 versus p = 0-0-1; the class column decides before order. Assumptions (same sheet, no layers, no !important) are stated. Only the filler hint and a thin note on option D hold it back.
evidence: knowledge: hand specificity — .card → 0-1-0, p → 0-0-1, total 0-1-1; p alone → 0-0-1; compare columns left to right: 0=0, 1>0 → .card p wins
node: rm-css-1 .card p = 0,1,1 vs p = 0,0,1
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Specificity — ID/CLASS/TYPE columns; at equal specificity "the last declared selector wins"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Cascade — criteria order: origin and importance, specificity, scoping proximity, order of appearance
knowledge: .card p = 0-1-1 (class .card 0-1-0 + type p 0-0-1); p = 0-0-1; class column decides
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_cascade/Cascade — 'Order of appearance: ... the last declaration in the style order is applied' comes after specificity
verification.notes: Hint now asks for id-class-type counts and the explanation covers the not-dropped distractor; all four checks hold.

items.objective: State what box-sizing: border-box changes: width and height include padding and border, never margin.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
items.rationale: Definition verified against MDN; distractors are real misconceptions (border inside padding, margins, display). Only the hint fails.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/box-sizing — border-box: "The width and height properties include the content, padding, and border, but do not include the margin"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/box-sizing — border-box: 'The width and height properties include the content, padding, and border, but do not include the margin'
knowledge: box-sizing does not affect margin collapsing, border painting position, or display
verification.notes: All three distractors are named and refuted in the explanation and the hint stays on the measurement question.

items.objective: Predict collapsed vertical margins between adjacent blocks in normal flow: the larger margin wins.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
items.rationale: Assumptions (stacked blocks, normal flow) are stated; the key (30px) and the flex/grid exception are verified against MDN. Hint only.
evidence: node: rm-css-11 collapsed gap = max(20,30) = 30 | sum would be 50

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_box_model/Mastering_margin_collapsing — adjacent siblings collapse "into a single margin whose size is the largest of the individual margins"; margins never collapse for floating, absolutely positioned, flex items, grid items; "only relevant in the vertical direction"

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_box_model/Mastering_margin_collapsing — 'The top and bottom margins of blocks are sometimes combined (collapsed) into a single margin whose size is the largest of the individual margins'
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_box_model/Mastering_margin_collapsing — 'Margins don't collapse in a container with display set to flex or grid'
verification.notes: max(20,30) = 30 is the only defensible option and the flex/grid exception in the explanation matches MDN.

items.objective: Explain why a percentage min-height needs a containing block with a definite height.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
distractor "The `display` value" is partly defensible (min-height does not apply to non-replaced inline elements)
explanation's "or with the parent made a flex or grid container" is loose — flex/grid make the child stretch; they do not make the percentage resolve
items.rationale: Key verified: MDN states the percentage is treated as 0 when the containing block's height is not specified. The display distractor is replaced and the flex/grid remark tightened.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/min-height — "The percentage is calculated with respect to the height of the generated box's containing block. If the height of the containing block is not specified explicitly (i.e., it depends on content height), and this element is not absolutely positioned, the percentage value is treated as 0"; "Applies to: all elements but non-replaced inline elements, table columns, and column groups"

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/min-height — 'The percentage is calculated with respect to the height of the generated box's containing block. If the height of the containing block is not specified explicitly (i.e., it depends on content height), and this element is not absolutely positioned, the percentage value is treated as 0'
verification.notes: The old display distractor is gone and the flex/grid remark now says stretching rather than resolving, which is the accurate mechanism.

items.objective: Choose overflow-wrap to break an unbreakable string rather than clipping or decorating the overflow.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
explanation does not say what `white-space: nowrap` would do
items.rationale: Key verified against MDN (anywhere breaks an otherwise unbreakable string); the three distractors are the usual wrong reflexes. Hint only.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/overflow-wrap — anywhere: "an otherwise unbreakable string of characters — like a long word or URL — may be broken at any point if there are no otherwise-acceptable break points in the line"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-overflow — "The text-overflow property doesn't force an overflow to occur … you have to set other CSS properties: overflow and white-space"

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/overflow-wrap — anywhere: 'an otherwise unbreakable string of characters ... may be broken at any point if there are no otherwise-acceptable break points in the line'
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-overflow — 'The text-overflow property doesn't force an overflow to occur ... you have to set other CSS properties: overflow and white-space'
verification.notes: The added `break-word` alternative and the nowrap sentence are both accurate; the hint sorts the properties by function without naming one.

items.objective: Diagnose horizontal page overflow by finding the element wider than the viewport instead of masking it.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
key option is a long two-clause sentence against short distractors
distractor "Reduce the base font size" is a throwaway
items.rationale: A judgement item, but the judgement is the standard one and the explanation gives the real cost of the wrong fix (unreachable content). Options need balancing.
evidence: knowledge: horizontal document scroll means some box's right edge exceeds the viewport width; overflow-x: hidden on body clips it without removing the cause

knowledge: a document scrolls horizontally when some box's inline-end edge exceeds the viewport width; overflow-x: hidden on body clips that box without removing the cause and can put content out of reach
knowledge: outline does not participate in layout, so `* { outline: 1px solid red }` reveals box edges without shifting them
verification.notes: Judgement item, but the three alternatives are guesses that never locate the offending element, so the key stands alone.

items.objective: Distinguish rem (root font size) from em (inherited font size) and why em compounds through nesting.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
key is markedly longer than the distractors (automated flag confirmed)
"`em` is absolute" is a throwaway distractor
items.rationale: Definitions verified against MDN; the compounding point is the transferable lesson. Options balanced, hint made specific.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/length — em: "If used on the font-size property itself, it represents the inherited font-size of the element"; rem: "Represents the font-size of the root element … user-defined preferences may modify this"
knowledge: 0.9^3 = 0.729

problems: hint eliminates every distractor: 'Both are relative' rules out the absolute option and 'which element's font size each one reads' rules out both identical and viewport
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/length — em: 'If used on the font-size property itself, it represents the inherited font-size of the element'; rem: 'Represents the font-size of the root element'
node: 0.9**3 = 0.7290000000000001, so three levels of 0.9em give 0.729 of the start
verification.notes: The replacement hint still points at compounding but leaves the four readings open.

items.objective: Understand what a percentage width on a flex item resolves against, and why flex sizing expresses the intent better than percentages.
defects: hint is the generic fallback

key claims the item "sizes against the parent rather than participating in the layout": a flex item with `width: 100%` does participate — the width becomes its flex basis and it shrinks by default (`flex-shrink: 1`)

"can overflow" holds only under unstated conditions (`flex-shrink: 0`, or `content-box` padding with a min-content floor); under `border-box`, which rm-css-9 recommends, `width: 100%` plus padding does not overflow at all
explanation's "`flex: 1` … cannot overflow the way this does" ignores the min-content floor (rm-css-20)
"often the wrong tool" is a judgement with its box-sizing assumption unstated
items.rationale: The objective (percentages vs flex sizing in a row) is worth keeping, but the item's mechanism claim is inaccurate as written and cannot be verified without a browser. The rewrite restates the scenario as a verifiable fact from MDN — what the percentage resolves against — and keeps the same lesson; the caller should note this is a fuller restatement than the other rewrites in the batch.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_flexible_box_layout/Controlling_ratios_of_flex_items_along_the_main_axis — "Percentage values are relative to the flex container's inner main size. If width: 50% were set, the flex-basis for this item would be half of the container's content-box width"; "The flex shrink factor is multiplied by the flex base size when distributing negative space"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex-shrink — initial value 1; negative free space "is distributed between the line's flex items that have a flex-shrink value greater than 0"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/gap — "There is no gutter before the first track or after the last track"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/box-sizing — border-box: width includes padding and border

knowledge: no headless browser is available in this environment (jsdom only, no layout), so the original's overflow claim could not be executed; the rewrite relies only on the documented resolution rule

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_flexible_box_layout/Controlling_ratios_of_flex_items_along_the_main_axis — 'Percentage values are relative to the flex container's inner main size. If width: 50% were set, the flex-basis for this item would be half of the container's content-box width'
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex-wrap — nowrap is the initial value, so the two items stay on one line and shrink or overflow
verification.notes: The rebuilt question asks a documented resolution fact instead of the original's unverifiable overflow claim, and the shrink/overflow sentence correctly hinges on flex-shrink's default of 1.

items.objective: Map justify-content to the main axis, which flex-direction: row makes horizontal.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
only the key carries the explanatory tail "which is horizontal here" — a length/detail clue
"The axis with more space" is a throwaway
items.rationale: Correct per MDN; the paired option shape (cross axis / main axis, each with its direction) removes the clue that only the key explained itself.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_flexible_box_layout/Basic_concepts_of_flexbox — row: main axis runs horizontally (inline direction); "justify-content: Aligns flex items along the main axis"; "align-items: Aligns flex items along the cross axis"

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_flexible_box_layout/Basic_concepts_of_flexbox — flex-direction: row puts the main axis along the inline direction; justify-content aligns along the main axis, align-items along the cross axis
knowledge: no CSS property aligns on both axes at once, and free space never selects the axis
verification.notes: The horizontal-writing-mode qualifier sits in the explanation rather than the question, but no other option claims the main axis so the key is still unique.

items.objective: Expand the flex: 1 shorthand (grow 1, shrink 1, basis 0%) and contrast it with flex: auto.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
items.rationale: Key matches MDN's one-value expansion (basis 0%); option D (1 0 auto) and B (grow only) are the genuine misconceptions. Hint only.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex — "One value, unitless number: flex-grow; flex-basis is then equal to 0%"; flex: auto "expands to flex: 1 1 auto"; flex: initial "expands to flex: 0 1 auto"

problems: hint eliminates every distractor: 'fills in two values you did not write' rules out the one-longhand and basis-only options, and 'items end up equal even when their content is not' rules out the flex-basis: auto option
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex — 'One value, unitless number: flex-grow ... flex-basis is then equal to 0%'; 'flex: auto; /* 1 1 auto */'; 'flex: initial; /* 0 1 auto */'
knowledge: the key and the flex-basis: auto distractor differ only in shrink and basis, which is the discrimination the old hint gave away
verification.notes: New hint keeps the three-longhand cue but leaves the basis 0% versus auto choice to the learner.

items.objective: Diagnose flex items overflowing instead of wrapping: flex-wrap defaults to nowrap.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
only the key carries an explanatory tail ("which is the default") — a detail clue
explanation does not say why the distractors fail
items.rationale: Default verified (nowrap, "may cause the flex container to overflow"). Giving option D the same "left at its default" shape removes the clue that only the key explained itself.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex-wrap — initial value nowrap: "The flex items are laid out in a single line which may cause the flex container to overflow"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex-wrap — Initial value nowrap: 'The flex items are laid out in a single line which may cause the flex container to overflow'
verification.notes: Both defaults now carry the same option shape, and the explanation refutes justify-content, align-items and the missing width.

items.objective: At equal specificity, the later declaration in source order wins (same origin, no layers, no !important).
defects: hint is the generic fallback
assumptions not stated: origin, layer and importance must also tie for order to decide
distractor "The one in the smaller file" is a throwaway
items.rationale: Correct and foundational; the question needs its tie conditions stated (MDN lists scoping proximity and origin/layer ahead of order) and a real distractor in place of "smaller file".
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Specificity — equal specificity: "Source order: The last declared selector wins"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Cascade — "Order of appearance — Last declaration in style order is applied", after origin/importance, specificity and scoping proximity

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_cascade/Cascade — 'Order of appearance: In the origin with precedence, if there are competing values ... of equal specificity and scoping proximity, the last declaration in the style order is applied'

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_cascade/Specificity — 'If scope proximity is also the same for both selectors, source order then comes into play. When all else is equal, the last selector wins.'
verification.notes: Tie conditions are now stated in the question and both new distractors (selector length, match count) are genuinely outside the cascade.

items.objective: Fix a flex item that will not shrink below its content by releasing the automatic minimum with min-width: 0.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
explanation does not say why `overflow: hidden` on the container (rather than the item) fails
items.rationale: One of the most-hit real bugs in flex layouts; key and the scroll-container exception verified against MDN's min-width: auto definition. Hint only.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/min-width — auto: "For flex items and grid items, the minimum width value is either the specified suggested size … otherwise, the min-content size is used. If the flex or grid item is a scroll container … the automatic minimum size is 0"

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/min-width — auto: 'For flex items and grid items, the minimum width value is either the specified suggested size ... otherwise, the min-content size is used. If the flex or grid item is a scroll container ... the automatic minimum size is 0'
verification.notes: overflow: hidden would work on the item but the distractor puts it on the container, which the explanation now says explicitly.

items.objective: Distinguish align-items (items within a line) from align-content (the lines themselves) in a wrapping flex container.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
key is markedly longer than the distractors
explanation only describes align-content's single-line behaviour and never states the contrast the question asks for
items.rationale: Key verified; MDN also confirms the single-line no-effect rule and that align-content applies beyond grid, so distractor C is false as intended.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/align-content — "sets the distribution of space between and around content items along a flexbox's cross axis, or a grid or block-level element's block axis"; "This property has no effect on single line flex containers (i.e., ones with flex-wrap: nowrap)"

problems: the question asks for the difference but only the key describes one, so the hint's framing ('two things to align: the items and the lines') hands over the answer by elimination
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/align-content — 'sets the distribution of space between and around content items along a flexbox's cross axis, or a grid or block-level element's block axis'; 'This property has no effect on single line flex containers'
knowledge: align-items aligns each item inside its own line, so the reversed mapping is false and makes a legitimate strongest distractor
verification.notes: Replacing the 'two names for one behaviour' throwaway with the reversed mapping makes the item test the mapping the hint asks the learner to work out.

items.objective: Prefer gap over margin hacks, spacer elements or space-between for a fixed spacing between flex items.
defects: hint is the generic fallback ("Identify the requirement or failure mode…")
items.rationale: Key verified (gap adds no outer gutters, works in flex); the four options are the four real approaches people use. Hint only.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/gap — "sets the gaps (also called gutters) between rows and columns on multi-column, flex, and grid containers"; "There is no gutter before the first track or after the last track"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/gap — 'There is no gutter before the first track or after the last track', and gap applies to multi-column, flex and grid containers
knowledge: justify-content: space-between distributes leftover space, so the spacing varies with container width instead of being fixed
verification.notes: Hint turns on the wrap case, which is exactly where the margin hack and the spacer approach fail.

items.objective: Stop a flex item (an icon) from shrinking with flex-shrink: 0 so the text absorbs the squeeze.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
explanation does not address the three distractors
items.rationale: Key verified (initial flex-shrink 1; items with 0 take no negative space). Hint and distractor coverage were the only gaps.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex-shrink — initial value 1; negative free space "is distributed between the line's flex items that have a flex-shrink value greater than 0"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex-shrink — initial value 1; negative free space 'is distributed between the line's flex items that have a flex-shrink value greater than 0'
verification.notes: The explanation now refutes align-items, flex-wrap and the container min-width, and the hint names a mechanism rather than an option.

items.objective: Choose Flexbox for one-dimensional, content-driven layouts and Grid for two-dimensional structures.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
key is markedly longer than the distractors
"When alignment is needed" is a thin distractor
items.rationale: Matches MDN's own decision rule (one dimension → flexbox; content-out vs layout-in). Options balanced to the same "when/whenever" shape.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_grid_layout/Relationship_of_grid_layout_with_other_layout_methods — "Flexbox works from the content out … Grid works from the layout in"; "Do we only need to control the layout by row or column? If yes, use flexbox"; "if you are setting a width on a flex item to make it line up with other items in a row above, a grid is likely a better choice"

problems: hint paraphrases the key: it names both of the key's clauses (how many dimensions, content versus a structure you define) and no distractor mentions either
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_grid_layout/Relationship_of_grid_layout_with_other_layout_methods — 'Do we only need to control the layout by row or column? If yes, use flexbox'; 'Flexbox works from the content out'; 'Grid works from the layout in'

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_grid_layout/Relationship_of_grid_layout_with_other_layout_methods — 'if you are setting a width on a flex item to make it line up with other items in a row above, a grid is likely a better choice'
verification.notes: New hint pushes back on the two throwaway distractors instead of restating the key's wording.

items.objective: Read repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)): as many columns of at least 200px as fit, sharing the leftover space.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
key is markedly longer than the distractors (automated flag confirmed)
items.rationale: The canonical media-query-free grid; behaviour verified against MDN's auto-fill/auto-fit and fr definitions. Options balanced, hint made structural.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/repeat — auto-fill: "Resolves to the largest number of repetitions that does not cause overflow"; auto-fit: "Behaves as auto-fill, except that after placing grid items, any empty repeated tracks are collapsed"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex_value — "The fr unit represents a fraction of the leftover space in the grid container"

problems: explanation claims 'the number of items never sets the count', which is false for auto-fit: after placement any empty repeated tracks are collapsed, so the rendered column count follows the items when they are fewer than the tracks that fit
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/repeat — auto-fit: 'Behaves as auto-fill, except that after placing grid items, any empty repeated tracks are collapsed'; auto-fill: 'Resolves to the largest number of repetitions that does not cause overflow'
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex_value — 'The fr unit represents a fraction of the leftover space in the grid container'
verification.notes: Key and hint are sound; only the sentence that overstates the item count needed correcting, and it now sets up rm-css-26.

items.objective: Distinguish auto-fit (collapses empty tracks so items stretch) from auto-fill (keeps them) when a row is short.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
key is markedly longer than the distractors (automated flag confirmed); "None" is a one-word option
items.rationale: Key verified word for word against MDN (auto-fit collapses empty repeated tracks to 0px). The reversed-roles distractor now mirrors the key's length.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/repeat — auto-fit: "after placing grid items, any empty repeated tracks are collapsed"; "A collapsed track is treated as having a single fixed track sizing function of 0px, and the gutters on either side of it collapse"

problems: key says the collapse makes items stretch, which holds only for a flexible track function: with `repeat(auto-fit, 250px)` the empty tracks still collapse but the items stay 250px
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/repeat — 'The auto-fit value behaves the same as auto-fill, except that after placing the grid items any empty repeated tracks are collapsed. An empty track is one with no in-flow grid items placed into or spanning across it.'
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex_value — fr distributes leftover space, which is what lets the surviving tracks take the collapsed tracks' width
verification.notes: Naming the track function in the question makes the stretch claim in the key and the explanation true as written.

items.objective: Understand that fr distributes the space left after fixed tracks and gaps are taken.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
items.rationale: Key verified against MDN and the Grid 2 spec (leftover space; gaps accounted for before fr). Hint only.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_grid_layout/Basic_concepts_of_grid_layout — "The first track is 500px, so the fixed width is taken away from the available space. The remaining space is divided into three"; "Any space used by gaps will be accounted for before space is assigned to the flexible length fr tracks"
https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/ — "A flexible length or <flex> is a dimension with the fr unit, which represents a fraction of the leftover space in the grid container"
https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/ — 'A flexible length or <flex> is a dimension with the fr unit, which represents a fraction of the leftover space in the grid container'

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_grid_layout/Basic_concepts_of_grid_layout — 'Any space used by gaps will be accounted for before space is assigned to the flexible length fr tracks'
verification.notes: Hint sets a concrete test case (`200px 1fr`) rather than restating the rule, and the explanation refutes all three distractors.

items.objective: Diagnose a grid track that will not shrink: 1fr means minmax(auto, 1fr) and the auto minimum is content-based; use minmax(0, 1fr).
defects: hint is the generic fallback
key is markedly longer than the distractors (automated flag confirmed); "`fr` does not shrink" is thin
"the single commonest grid bug" is an unsupported superlative
items.rationale: Mechanism verified in the Grid 2 spec (implied minmax(auto, <flex>); auto minimum = largest minimum size of the items) and MDN's min-width: auto for grid items. Complements rm-css-20 rather than duplicating it.
evidence: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/ — <flex>: "When appearing outside a minmax() notation, implies an automatic minimum (i.e. minmax(auto, <flex>))"; auto as minimum: "represents the largest minimum size (specified by min-width/min-height) of the grid items occupying the grid track"
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/min-width — for flex items and grid items auto resolves to the specified size, transferred size, "otherwise, the min-content size is used"
https://www.w3.org/TR/css-grid-2/ — <flex> 'When appearing outside a minmax() notation, implies an automatic minimum (i.e. minmax(auto, <flex>))'
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/min-width — for flex and grid items auto resolves to the specified or transferred size, 'otherwise, the min-content size is used'
verification.notes: Mechanism is spec-accurate, the unsupported superlative is gone, and it complements rather than duplicates the flex version in rm-css-20.

items.objective: Choose breakpoints where the layout stops working rather than from device sizes.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
"What is the better basis?" presupposes the premise is worse — mildly leading
items.rationale: Guidance rather than a spec fact, but it is MDN's guidance and the options all share one shape. The leading "better basis" phrasing is left; the hint and explanation carry the reasoning.
evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/CSS_layout/Responsive_Design — "if a box becomes squashed with two words on each line as it narrows you can set a breakpoint"; layouts based on content rather than specific devices

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/CSS_layout/Responsive_Design — breakpoints are set where the content stops working, e.g. 'if a box becomes squashed with two words on each line as it narrows you can set a breakpoint'
verification.notes: Guidance item rather than a spec fact; it passes both gates at the reviewer's scores and the hint leaves the arbitrary-number option open.

items.objective: Understand that !important changes a declaration's importance/origin rank in the cascade, not its specificity.
defects: hint is the generic fallback
key option is a 15-word sentence against 3–5-word distractors (automated flag confirmed)
key understates the rule: an important author declaration outranks normal declarations from every origin, not only its own
items.rationale: The concept is right (importance is sorted before specificity), but the key is both conspicuously long and slightly narrower than the rule. Balanced options and a precise explanation fix it.
